explanation: In Greece, pointing with the index finger is generally considered impolite or aggressive, especially in formal or traditional settings, as it can be seen as a confrontational gesture. Greeks often prefer to point with their whole hand or a nod of the head to indicate direction or a person. This caution is rooted in cultural norms that value indirectness and respect for personal space in everyday interactions.
local_tip: Instead of pointing, gesture with an open hand or tilt your head in the intended direction to avoid giving offense.
regional_note: In more cosmopolitan areas like Athens, younger generations may be more tolerant of index finger pointing, but it remains risky in rural or older circles.

also_check.note: Pointing with the index finger is considered very rude; use an open hand or a gentle nod instead.
Pointing with the index finger is taboo, especially with the left hand; use the thumb or an open palm.
Index finger pointing is common and generally acceptable in casual contexts, though it can be seen as blunt in formal settings.
